name: Apple Custard
description: Historical recipe from Miss Leslie's Complete Cookery (1851). Source method; not modernized or kitchen-tested.

ingredients.name: yellow peel of a large lemon
ingredients.originalText: yellow peel of a large lemon

ingredients.name: quarter of a pound of sugar
ingredients.originalText: a quarter of a pound of sugar

instructions.text: Pare, core, and quarter a dozen large juicy pippins
Strew among them the yellow peel of a large lemon grated very fine
Stew them till tender, in a very small portion of water
When done, mash them smooth with the back of a spoon
Mix a quarter of a pound of sugar with them, and set them away till cold
Beat six eggs very light, and stir them gradually into a quart of rich milk, alternately with the stewed apple
Put the mixture into cups, or into a deep dish, and bake it about twenty minutes
Send it to table cold, with nutmeg grated over the top

source.author: Eliza Leslie
source.originalInstructions:
1. Pare, core, and quarter a dozen large juicy pippins
2. Strew among them the yellow peel of a large lemon grated very fine
3. Stew them till tender, in a very small portion of water
4. When done, mash them smooth with the back of a spoon
5. Mix a quarter of a pound of sugar with them, and set them away till cold
6. Beat six eggs very light, and stir them gradually into a quart of rich milk, alternately with the stewed apple
7. Put the mixture into cups, or into a deep dish, and bake it about twenty minutes
8. Send it to table cold, with nutmeg grated over the top
